So this row warms the npx package and wires it into Claude Code (if the `claude` CLI is present); it does NOT add a SweK panel button, because SweK has no MCP client. To attach it to the ACTUAL running engine page instead of a fresh tab, launch Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222 and add --browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222 to the MCP args. Requires Node LTS + Google Chrome (stable or newer).

gltfpack.description: gltfpack (zeux/meshoptimizer, MIT) - the CLI that shrinks .glb/.gltf/.obj models and makes them faster to render: vertex-cache + vertex-fetch optimization, quantization (KHR_mesh_quantization), mesh merging to cut draw calls, optional simplification (-si) for LODs, and EXT_meshopt_compression (-c/-cc) to slash download size. Directly relevant to SweK's asset pipeline - run it over the big models in your assets folder (the ~400 MB mech is exhibit A) to cut load time and GPU cost. Usage: `gltfpack -i in.glb -o out.glb` (add -cc for compressed output, -si 0.5 to simplify to ~50% tris, -tc for KTX2 textures). NOTE: the npm build is easiest but the native binary from the Releases page is faster and is the only one that does texture compression. RUNTIME CAVEAT: loading -c/-cc compressed .glb needs an EXT_meshopt_compression decoder wired into SweK's glTF loader (meshoptimizer ships js/meshopt_decoder.js) - plain -cc without that decoder will not load, so start with the lossless optimize/quantize pass (no -c) which any loader reads, then we can wire the decoder as a follow-on if you want the compressed path.
cmdsMac: npm install -g gltfpack
gltfpack -h

py-diso.description: SOURCE BUILD: diso (SarahWeiii) — Dual Marching Cubes CUDA extension (cumc.cu / cudualmc.cu) that ComfyUI-3D-Pack's install.py builds for fast voxel->mesh surface extraction. This is the sub-build that makes 'node-comfy3d-pack' fail. CONFIRMED BUILT MANUALLY on this rig: diso\\_C.pyd loaded ('Success! Loaded extension'). ROOT CAUSE (same family as py-cubvh): the portable's VS BuildTools 18 ships MSVC 14.51.36231, which CUDA 12.6 nvcc REJECTS (crt/host_config.h: only VS 2017-2022 supported). Adding --allow-unsupported-compiler bypasses the version gate but then cudafe++ crashes with 0xC0000005 (ACCESS_VIOLATION) on the v18 headers, so Option-1 (NVCC_FLAGS only) does NOT finish. The automated pip path (even via vcvars64 + DISTUTILS_USE_SDK=1 + --no-build-isolation) also does NOT work here. THE FIX that worked was a fully MANUAL x64 build: (0) open an x64 dev shell via vcvars64.bat; (1) nvcc-compile cumc.cu and cudualmc.cu to .obj with CCBIN forced to the OLDER MSVC 14.44.35207 Hostx64 x64 toolset + --allow-unsupported-compiler + -gencode arch=compute_61,code=sm_61 (Pascal / GTX 1070); (2) cl-compile src\\pybind.cpp WITHOUT defining _WINDLL (that macro forced __declspec(dllimport) on torch's pybind casters -> unresolved-symbol / instantiation errors); (3) link.exe the three .obj into diso\\_C.pyd against torch.lib torch_cpu.lib torch_cuda.lib c10.lib c10_cuda.lib cuda.lib cudart.lib AND torch_python.lib (the missing torch_python.lib was the other half of the link failure); (4) copy the built diso\\ folder (__init__.py + _C.pyd) into python_embeded\\Lib\\site-packages. manual:true — the cmd only ECHOES this recipe; run it yourself in an x64 Developer PowerShell. Transcribed from a verified build log; not re-verifiable from the bridge.
cmds: $pe='C:\\VoxelBAK\\ComfyUI_windows_portable\\python_embeded'; $py=$pe+'\\python.exe'; & $py -c 'import diso._C' 2>$null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Write-Host 'diso._C already importable - nothing to do'; exit 0 }; Write-Host 'diso must be built MANUALLY on this rig (VS18 / MSVC 14.51 vs CUDA 12.6 nvcc). Steps below run in an x64 Developer PowerShell:' -ForegroundColor Yellow; Write-Host '  0a) git clone https://github.com/SarahWeiii/diso.git C:\\diso_manual ; cd C:\\diso_manual'; Write-Host '  0b) start an x64 build env first:  call "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\18\\BuildTools\\VC\\Auxiliary\\Build\\vcvars64.bat"  (or open the x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS)'; Write-Host '  0c) set PythonEmbed=C:\\VoxelBAK\\ComfyUI_windows_portable\\python_embeded'; Write-Host '      set TorchInc=%PythonEmbed%\\Lib\\site-packages\\torch\\include'; Write-Host '      set CudaInc=C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v12.6\\include'; Write-Host '  1) nvcc -c src\\cumc.cu src\\cudualmc.cu  -ccbin "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\18\\BuildTools\\VC\\Tools\\MSVC\\14.44.35207\\bin\\Hostx64\\x64"  --allow-unsupported-compiler  -gencode=arch=compute_61,code=sm_61  -std=c++17   (plus the same -I / -D torch+cuda flags ComfyUI-3D-Pack already prints in its failed build line)'; Write-Host '  2) cl.exe /c src\\pybind.cpp /Fopybind.obj /O2 /std:c++17 /MD /DWITH_CUDA /Isrc /I"%TorchInc%" /I"%TorchInc%\\torch\\csrc\\api\\include" /I"%PythonEmbed%\\include" /I"%CudaInc%" /D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0 /DTORCH_EXTENSION_NAME=_C /DTORCH_API_INCLUDE_EXTENSION_H        <-- do NOT define _WINDLL'; Write-Host '  3) link.exe /DLL /OUT:diso\\_C.pyd pybind.obj cumc.obj cudualmc.obj /LIBPATH:"%PythonEmbed%\\libs" /LIBPATH:"%PythonEmbed%\\Lib\\site-packages\\torch\\lib" /LIBPATH:"C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v12.6\\lib\\x64" torch.lib torch_cpu.lib torch_cuda.lib c10.lib c10_cuda.lib cuda.lib cudart.lib torch_python.lib'; Write-Host '  4) copy C:\\diso_manual\\diso  ->  %PythonEmbed%\\Lib\\site-packages\\diso   then verify:  & $py -c "import diso._C; print(diso._C)"'

turbo-fieldfare.description: TurboFieldfare (drumih/turbo-fieldfare) - Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in about 2 GB of RAM, Swift + Metal, no npm. The model is 14.3 GB on disk but only a ~1.35 GB shared core stays resident plus the KV cache: it is a mixture-of-experts with 4B active params, so cold experts are paged on demand behind an LFU cache. Same trade as this engine's RLE volume cache and brick map - do not hold what you are not looking at - and its installer never materialises the full checkpoint, streaming byte ranges and repacking into .gturbo as they arrive, which is our .part discipline at 15 GB scale. *** IT CANNOT RUN ON STELLAR ATLAS. *** The package is pure arm64 and depends on Metal, so it needs APPLE SILICON; Stellar Atlas is an Intel Mac and no macOS upgrade changes that. It also needs macOS 26 with Metal 4, Xcode 26 and Swift 6.2. The only fleet machine that could run it is the M-series Mac - which is remote over the Cloudflare tunnel, and TurboFieldfare's own docs bind its OpenAI-compatible server to 127.0.0.1 with no auth and no TLS and say not to expose it through a proxy or tunnel. So the one box that qualifies is the one box we would have to reach the forbidden way. THIS ROW THEREFORE REFUSES BY NAME rather than offering an install that must fail: it reports which requirement the machine missed. Verified against the repo v3331.
cmds: Write-Host 'TurboFieldfare is macOS + Apple Silicon only (pure arm64 + Metal). Not for this Windows rig.'; exit 1
cmdsMac: arch=$(uname -m); osv=$(sw_vers -productVersion 2>/dev/null || echo 0); maj=${osv%%.*}; fail=0; if [ "$arch" != "arm64" ]; then echo "REFUSED: needs Apple Silicon (arm64); this Mac reports $arch. Stellar Atlas is Intel -- this is an ARCHITECTURE refusal, not an OS-version one."; fail=1; fi; if [ "$maj" -lt 26 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "REFUSED: needs macOS 26 (Metal 4); this Mac reports $osv."; fail=1; fi; if ! command -v swift >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "REFUSED: needs Swift 6.2 (Xcode 26); no swift on PATH."; fail=1; fi; if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then echo 'Nothing was installed. Each line above names the requirement that was missed.'; exit 1; fi; echo 'All requirements met. Manual from here: git clone https://github.com/drumih/turbo-fieldfare.git && cd turbo-fieldfare && swift build -c release'

requires.why: Pure arm64 and depends on Metal, and needs macOS 26 with Metal 4. Stellar Atlas is an Intel Mac, so this is an ARCHITECTURE refusal there, not a version one.

ardy.description:
ARDY (nv-tlabs/ardy) - HONEST PLACEHOLDER, NOT WIRED. NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab's 'Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation' (SIGGRAPH 2026 / ACM TOG). *** TWO CORRECTIONS ARE RECORDED HERE BECAUSE BOTH WERE MADE. (1) IT WAS RAISED AS 'aero-ex/Ardy'. Aero-Ex is a REAL user who FORKS NVIDIA work (their kimodo is forked from nv-tlabs/kimodo; they also publish Nvidia_MotionBricks and ComfyUI-Trellis2-GGUF) -- so the name came from somewhere real, but the repo is nv-tlabs/ardy. RIGHT MODEL, WRONG OWNER. (2) IT IS NOT A RENDER MODEL. It generates 3D human and humanoid MOTION from text, streaming frame by frame with masked kinematic constraints -- ANIMATION, NOT PIXELS. Nothing about it belongs in a render pipeline; if it belongs anywhere in SweK it is as a MOTION SOURCE feeding ragdoll / box3d / RagdollDismember, which is a different subsystem with a different question. ***
WHY THERE IS NO INSTALL COMMAND: it fails the bar four ways -- conda env, `pip install -e ".[all]"`, PyTorch matched to your CUDA installed FIRST, and a [trt] extra needing NVIDIA driver >= 525 plus pypi.nvidia.com. And the one that is a different CLASS of blocker: THE TEXT ENCODER RELIES ON THE GATED meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, which needs an APPROVED HuggingFace account and a token at runtime. A dependency that requires somebody's PERMISSION is not the same as a big download, and no install command can paper over it. HARDWARE, UNMEASURED AND THEREFORE UNDECLARED: tested on Ubuntu 22.04 with an RTX 4090 and driver 575. Galaxina is Pascal / sm_61 with 8 GB, and an 8B Llama encoder beside a diffusion model is the real question. *** `requires` IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OFF UNTIL SOMEBODY MEASURES IT -- declaring a constraint that has not been read or measured is exactly what VERIFY_EXTERNAL item 5 forbids. *** LICENSING IS SPLIT: inference code Apache 2.0; MODEL WEIGHTS under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use permitted WITH ATTRIBUTION, own redistribution terms, NOT Apache and NOT CC-BY) - review the weight licence separately. Related NVIDIA work its own README names, if the motion question is ever taken up: Kimodo (offline authoring), MotionBricks (real-time in-betweening), GEAR SONIC (ARDY can act as a PLANNER feeding it; they drove a Unitree G1). Verified against the repo v3336. No fabricated install command.
cmds: Write-Host 'ARDY is a PLACEHOLDER row - nothing is wired. Repo: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/ardy  (NOT aero-ex). It generates MOTION, not pixels, and its text encoder needs approved access to a gated Llama-3-8B. Read the description before installing anything by hand.'

requires.why: READ v3336, CONSTRAINT REAL AND NOT YET MEASURED -- which is a THIRD state, not the read-and-unconstrained one. ARDY is tested on Ubuntu 22.04 with an RTX 4090; Galaxina is Pascal/sm_61 with 8 GB, and an 8B Llama text encoder beside a diffusion model is the open question. Declaring os/arch here would be fabricating a constraint nobody has run; declaring nothing would claim it runs. It refuses until somebody measures it, and the refusal names why.

node3d-gl.description: @node-3d native OpenGL for Node (MIT) -- a REAL DESKTOP GL WINDOW driven from Node, not a browser tab. @node-3d/core pulls webgl + glfw + image; all five packages are MIT with LICENSE files. NO COMPILER IS NEEDED: each install.js downloads a PREBUILT binary from its own GitHub Releases (measured on linux-x64: 4 packages, 3 seconds, ~7 MB, no node-gyp). *** IT IS NOT HEADLESS. *** GLFW needs a display server -- on a headless box it fails with 'GLFW Error 65550: Failed to detect any supported platform', so this does NOT replace the headless Chromium the shader gates use. Install it to open a native window, not to speed up CI. PLATFORMS: prebuilts exist for win32-x64, linux-x64, darwin-x64 and linux-arm64 ONLY -- APPLE SILICON (darwin-arm64) HAS NO BUILD and the row refuses it rather than recommending it. Packages ask for node >=24.13.0 / npm >=11.6.2 (npm warns EBADENGINE; not enforced -- it loaded on node 22). See world/nodeGlPlatforms.mjs for what was measured here versus read upstream.

requires.why: @node-3d ships prebuilt binaries only, for four platform/arch pairs. Neither ARM desktop pair has a @node-3d prebuilt: Apple Silicon (darwin-arm64) and Windows on ARM (win32-arm64) both fall outside the map, while linux-arm64 is inside it -- so this is not 'ARM is unsupported', it is three specific OS-and-chip combinations that were built and one pair per OS that was not. Not an OS-version problem and not fixable by upgrading; the binary does not exist. Intel Macs (darwin-x64) and x64 Windows are supported.
